speaker: Steve Holmes
sentence: Dylan is probably my favorite artist of all time.

speaker: arcade-fire
sentence: It was New Order, Debussy, Arvo Part, the Pixies.

speaker: at-the-drive-in
sentence: I learned to play bass by playing along with the Pixies and Dead Kennedys.
citation: Jim Ward of At the Drive-In and Sparta, in Spin's "5 Albums I Can't Live Without" (2026): "I learned to play bass by playing along with the Pixies and Dead Kennedys."
note: Said in the intro answers, not under a pick.

speaker: Stuart Murdoch of Belle and Sebastian
sentence: It had a great effect on me at the time, but I don’t listen to The Fall very often now. It went along with my abrasive nature at the time – this crazy ranter, Mark E Smith, appealed to me deeply.
citation: Stuart Murdoch of Belle and Sebastian, choosing The Fall's This Nation's Saving Grace for The Quietus's Baker's Dozen: "It had a great effect on me at the time, but I don't listen to The Fall very often now."
note: marginal: effect on him as a young listener, not on his songwriting

speaker: Steve Albini
sentence: My favorite bands during that era include those mentioned above, and local/regional bands that inspired me like Naked Raygun, the Effigies, the Appliances, Killdozer, Die Kreuzen, Bad Brains, the Minutemen, Scrawl, Man-Sized Action, the Blackouts, MX-80, Chrome and a bunch of overseas bands like the Birthday Party, Killing Joke, the Bishops, Dr. Feelgood, the Raincoats, Kleenex, Delta Five, Ut, Contortions, Sonic Youth, Swans, Public Image Ltd, This Heat.

speaker: Steve Albini
sentence: My favorite bands during that era include those mentioned above, and local/regional bands that inspired me like Naked Raygun, the Effigies, the Appliances, Killdozer, Die Kreuzen, Bad Brains, the Minutemen, Scrawl, Man-Sized Action, the Blackouts, MX-80, Chrome and a bunch of overseas bands like the Birthday Party, Killing Joke, the Bishops, Dr. Feelgood, the Raincoats, Kleenex, Delta Five, Ut, Contortions, Sonic Youth, Swans, Public Image Ltd, This Heat.

speaker: black-flag
sentence: Alan Vega was a hero to me growing up because of the first Suicide record.
citation: Henry Rollins, in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2019): "Alan Vega was a hero to me growing up because of the first Suicide record."
note: Hero "growing up" (before Black Flag); Rollins Band later covered "Ghost Rider".

speaker: blonde-redhead
sentence: I never said it, but I felt like I was their student.
citation: Kazu Makino, in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2023): "I never said it, but I felt like I was their student."
note: Also says "I really felt like the earth was shaking when I heard Unwound"; toured with them from 1995.

speaker: Graham Coxon
sentence: Yo La Tengo and Pavement were also great encouragement to do whatever I wanted when I had the space.

speaker: Brian Eno
sentence: It doesn’t have to be this person at the front with all the articulation and every word clear. It can just be a person in that mess and that was a real liberation for me.
citation: Brian Eno, choosing Glider by My Bloody Valentine for The Quietus's Baker's Dozen: "One of the things that I really love in that is the fact that there's singing in there but you have no idea what it's doing... that was a real liberation for me." He says the experience of hearing it "has a lot to do with what I'm doing now".

speaker: Steve Diggle of Buzzcocks
sentence: Bowie was an inspiration to [Buzzcocks] like The Beatles were.
citation: Steve Diggle of Buzzcocks, choosing David Bowie's 'Panic In Detroit' for The Quietus's Baker's Dozen: "Bowie was an inspiration to [Buzzcocks] like The Beatles were."

speaker: Dan Snaith of Caribou
sentence: People who know my albums from ten years ago will have heard me trying to rip off Silver Apples.
citation: Dan Snaith of Caribou, choosing Silver Apples' debut for The Quietus's Baker's Dozen: "People who know my albums from ten years ago will have heard me trying to rip off Silver Apples."

speaker: Chan Marshall (Cat Power)
sentence: Loved Bob. Loved him. ‘Tangled Up In Blue’ was fucking watershed for me.
citation: Chan Marshall (Cat Power), choosing Bob Dylan's Desire for The Quietus's Baker's Dozen: "Loved Bob. Loved him. 'Tangled Up In Blue' was fucking watershed for me."

speaker: descendents
sentence: Bad Brains had put out the “Pay to Cum” single in 1980, and that had a huge effect on us.
citation: Milo Aukerman, in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2016): "Bad Brains had put out the 'Pay to Cum' single in 1980, and that had a huge effect on us."
note: "We wanted to play as fast as humanly possible but still be tight."

speaker: destroyer
sentence: When Slanted and Enchanted came out, everything changed.
citation: Dan Bejar, in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2012): "When Slanted and Enchanted came out, everything changed."
note: Also: "That's when I bought an electric guitar and an amplifier. I was 21."

speaker: Rick Froberg to Vish Khanna, 2005
sentence: I’m sure we aped Fugazi, who we were big fans of.

speaker: Ian McCulloch of Echo & the Bunnymen
sentence: He flips it round – it’s what I do a lot.
citation: Ian McCulloch of Echo & the Bunnymen, choosing The Best Of Leonard Cohen by Leonard Cohen for The Quietus's Baker's Dozen: "Bowie got me looking out the window... but what Cohen does is he turns me into him." He bought all his albums at 14, and of the way Cohen turns lyrics on their head: "it's what I do a lot."

speaker: Tom Smith
sentence: “Obviously, we're dark and moody so yeah we build on the sound of the likes of Joy Division, Echo and the Bunnymen and The Chameleons… Obviously we were too young when these bands came out, so it's only more recently that we discovered them.”

speaker: Robin Pecknold
sentence: Lots of Nic Jones, Beach House, Roy Harper, Dungen, Joanna Newsom, West Coast Pop Art Experimental Band.

speaker: Gary Numan
sentence: It’s a huge album for me and re-kindled my love of darker music. It’s a massively important album and it helped to massively change my own direction and I’ve been going out in that direction ever since.
citation: Gary Numan, choosing Songs Of Faith And Devotion by Depeche Mode for The Quietus's Baker's Dozen: "It's a massively important album and it helped to massively change my own direction and I've been going out in that direction ever since."
note: Songs of Faith and Devotion (1993) shaped his later work, Sacrifice onwards.

speaker: Dallas Observer (on Jim Suptic)
sentence: Given the fact that his high school band, Kingpin, was heavily influenced by Slint, The Jesus Lizard and bands on the Amphetamine Reptile label, it comes as no surprise what show he saw first with his own money.

speaker: guided-by-voices
sentence: 154 was a bolt of lightning. When we started, we wanted to sound like a bunch of different bands.
citation: Robert Pollard of Guided by Voices, choosing Wire's 154 for Spin's "The Records That Changed My Life" (2004): "154 was a bolt of lightning. When we started, we wanted to sound like a bunch of different bands. The songs were going to be short, sound like they were recorded in a bunch of different places. That was the Wire influence."
note: found is two sentences; the third ("The songs were going to be short... That was the Wire influence.") finishes the claim and is quoted in the citation.

speaker: Bob Mould of Hüsker Dü
sentence: Then you’re stuck and you can’t get out of it. I take that lesson and I put it on my own stuff.
citation: Bob Mould of Hüsker Dü, choosing Unknown Pleasures by Joy Division for The Quietus's Baker's Dozen: "by the end of side one I was like, 'This is it, this is what we're gonna do with music now'... I take that lesson and I put it on my own stuff."

speaker: Michelle Zauner of Japanese Breakfast
sentence: Musicians like her and Kimya Dawson had these very singular voices that were great for me. I loved their songwriting and the character in it and sort of gave me the courage to be a singer without sounding like Aretha Franklin or something.
citation: Michelle Zauner of Japanese Breakfast, choosing Joanna Newsom's Ys for The Quietus's Baker's Dozen, said Newsom's songwriting "sort of gave me the courage to be a singer without sounding like Aretha Franklin or something."

speaker: Joanna Newsom
sentence: I love Donovan, Kate Bush, Leonard Cohen. Dylan, of course.

speaker: lcd-soundsystem
sentence: Between the age of 13 and 16 I liked The Clash, Bowie, Echo And The Bunnymen, The Cure, The Smiths, Sisters Of Mercy, Joy Division and New Order.

speaker: James Murphy
sentence: Between the age of 13 and 16 I liked The Clash, Bowie, Echo And The Bunnymen, The Cure, The Smiths, Sisters Of Mercy, Joy Division and New Order.

speaker: Alan Sparhawk
sentence: I remember having to force myself to not listen to Codeine and Red House Painters sometimes when I was writing, because I’d find myself falling too easily into their mannerisms and phrasings.

speaker: Mary Timony
sentence: My brother was really into classic rock, so I learned about the Beatles and the Stones and Brian Eno from him.

speaker: Robert Del Naja
sentence: PiL were a major influence on me with what they went for on Metal Box, and The Clash were really important as well.

speaker: mogwai
sentence: The bands that I was really excited by were things like Jimi Hendrix and The Velvet Underground and quite simple stuff like The Cure and The Jesus and Mary Chain.

speaker: mogwai
sentence: We were interested in a lot of American rock bands like Sonic Youth and Slint, as well as 70s guitar bands like the Stooges and Television.
citation: Stuart Braithwaite, in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2011): "We were interested in a lot of American rock bands like Sonic Youth and Slint, as well as 70s guitar bands like the Stooges and Television."
note: As for Sonic Youth.

speaker: Stephen Morris of New Order
sentence: I used to make cassettes of Tago Mago and go and sit in a field – I don’t know why – to play it there in the middle of the night, because it seemed like the best way to listen to it. I wasn’t very old; 13 or 14, playing Tago Mago in a field on my own with a cassette player running out of battery.
citation: Stephen Morris of New Order, choosing Can's Tago Mago for The Quietus's Baker's Dozen: "I used to make cassettes of Tago Mago and go and sit in a field... I wasn't very old; 13 or 14"
note: marginal: obsessive formative-years listening, nothing explicit about their own music

speaker: of-montreal
sentence: I saw what was possible, like, if these guys can do it, I can too.
citation: Kevin Barnes, in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2010): "I saw what was possible, like, if these guys can do it, I can too."
note: As for Neutral Milk Hotel.

speaker: perfume-genius
sentence: And then to hear someone else having that same feeling but then forming it into something really beautiful and honest…it was very powerful to me and became the soundtrack to that time in my life.

speaker: Mike Hadreas (Perfume Genius)
sentence: I count the cover as an influence. She’s defiant but not overt.
citation: Mike Hadreas (Perfume Genius), choosing Patti Smith's Horses for The Quietus's Baker's Dozen: "I count the cover as an influence."

speaker: Geoff Barrow of Portishead
sentence: Can are my favourite and most inspirational band ever, I think.
citation: Geoff Barrow of Portishead, choosing Ege Bamyasi by Can for The Quietus's Baker's Dozen: "Can are my favourite and most inspirational band ever, I think."

speaker: rem
sentence: There were all these records that came out around then that were so profoundly important.
citation: Michael Stipe, in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2021): "There were all these records that came out around then that were so profoundly important."
note: Said as R.E.M. were forming (1980); the B-52's told them "You gotta hear this unbelievable record by this band called Joy Division."

speaker: Andy Bell of Ride
sentence: I’ve taken on board a lot from David Roback’s guitar playing. It’s kind of Doorsy.
citation: Andy Bell of Ride, choosing She Hangs Brightly by Mazzy Star for The Quietus's Baker's Dozen: "I've taken on board a lot from David Roback's guitar playing."
note: Roback of Mazzy Star; She Hangs Brightly (1990) came after Ride formed, but he says he took the playing on board.

speaker: sharon-van-etten
sentence: My friend Paul played me this when I was in college, and it just killed me. It was so different, so minimal, and their voices together [Alan Sparhawk and Mimi Parker] were just beautiful.
citation: Sharon Van Etten, in the Observer's Soundtrack of My Life (2015): on Low's Two-Step: "My friend Paul played me this when I was in college, and it just killed me. It was so different, so minimal, and their voices together ... were just beautiful."

speaker: Neil Halstead of Slowdive
sentence: That album really hit me and it made me aware of music that wasn’t just a wall of guitars. It didn’t have an immediate impact on the way I wrote but it embedded itself in me.
citation: Neil Halstead of Slowdive, choosing Songs of Love and Hate by Leonard Cohen for The Quietus's Baker's Dozen: "We were listening to this a lot when Slowdive were recording Just For A Day... That album really hit me and it made me aware of music that wasn't just a wall of guitars."
note: He adds it had no immediate impact on the way he wrote; borderline.

speaker: Lee Ranaldo of Sonic Youth
sentence: Cohen’s another person I just constantly go back to for inspiration, especially these days as I’m writing more songs on my own and playing more acoustic guitar and getting deeper and deeper into the acoustic guitar.
citation: Lee Ranaldo of Sonic Youth, choosing Songs Of Love And Hate by Leonard Cohen for The Quietus's Baker's Dozen: "Cohen's another person I just constantly go back to for inspiration, especially these days as I'm writing more songs on my own."

speaker: sonic-youth
sentence: There was a time when I could play almost every song on that record on my guitar.
citation: Lee Ranaldo, in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2012): "There was a time when I could play almost every song on that record on my guitar."
note: After the Gold Rush; "In many ways, he set the tone for acoustic guitar players."

speaker: sonic-youth
sentence: Nobody else in the band gave a rat’s ass about Sparks! So we really connected – we were Sparks fanatics.
citation: Thurston Moore, in NME's Soundtrack Of My Life (2025): "I was really into Sparks. Nobody else in the band gave a rat's ass about Sparks! So we really connected – we were Sparks fanatics."
note: Fandom during his Sonic Youth years (Jim O'Rourke era), not a formative-years claim; borderline, owner may prefer favourite.

speaker: spoon
sentence: The Violent Femmes were probably the biggest band for me in that burst of new freedom, I just completely related to their lyrics. The lyrics speak to the minds of high school students like no other record – insecurity, anger, masturbation, frustration and lust.
citation: Britt Daniel of Spoon, in NME's Soundtrack Of My Life (2020), on 'Kiss Off' as the song that changed his life: "The Violent Femmes were probably the biggest band for me in that burst of new freedom, I just completely related to their lyrics."

speaker: Michael Gira
sentence: I listened to a wide variety of music then ­ The Stooges, Suicide, Throbbing Grist"le, SPK, Cabaret Voltaire, Whitehouse, Brian Eno, Kraftwerk, No New York , Wire, Sex Pistols, Buzzcocks, Black Flag.

speaker: Michael Gira

speaker: Michael Gira
sentence: I listened to a wide variety of music then ­ The Stooges, Suicide, Throbbing Grist"le, SPK, Cabaret Voltaire, Whitehouse, Brian Eno, Kraftwerk, No New York , Wire, Sex Pistols, Buzzcocks, Black Flag.

speaker: Paul Buchanan
sentence: But there were some great things. The Clash. The Pistols, the Talking Heads, and Television. I suppose we were at the right age as well.

speaker: Lol Tolhurst of The Cure
sentence: What I always thought of with the drums was once the rhythm’s there, there’s this whole space inside of it that you can listen to and focus on with the push and pull. That’s what I was always trying for.
citation: Lol Tolhurst of The Cure, choosing Can's Tago Mago for The Quietus's Baker's Dozen, on Jaki Liebezeit's drumming: "there's this whole space inside of it that you can listen to and focus on with the push and pull. That's what I was always trying for."
note: Moderate: about drumming approach rather than the record itself; he also names Can alongside Cluster in his Low pick.

speaker: the-human-league
sentence: Ware began speaking about the early electronic scene in Sheffield emerging from the industrial noise of the city, meeting Ian Craig Marsh in a youth project called Meat Whistle and going to see Roxy Music at Sheffield University, with Brian Eno specifically influencing his interest in making music.

speaker: the-postal-service
sentence: So yeah, her music definitely influenced the songs on the album.

speaker: The Radio Dept. (band site)
sentence: INFLUENCES (the band's own list on its 2007 site)

speaker: The Radio Dept. (band site)
sentence: INFLUENCES (the band's own list on its 2007 site)

speaker: Johnny Marr of The Smiths
sentence: with me being a teenager during the 70s meant I never stopped being affected by Brian’s music.
citation: Johnny Marr of The Smiths, choosing Brian Eno's Taking Tiger Mountain (By Strategy) for The Quietus's Baker's Dozen: "with me being a teenager during the 70s meant I never stopped being affected by Brian's music"
note: marginal: general effect of Eno's music on him as a teenager; the Taking Tiger Mountain remarks are about the record's reach

speaker: Justin Trosper (Unwound)
sentence: Yeah, VU and Sonic Youth are big influences.

speaker: vampire-weekend
sentence: I was already really into the first album.
citation: Ezra Koenig, in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2010): "I was already really into the first album."
note: Fan and briefly intern at the Walkmen's studio before Vampire Weekend: "I was really obsessed."

speaker: Xandy Chelmis
sentence: I really loved The Shins, Grizzly Bear, Real Estate, Beach Fossils, and Fleet Foxes was a big one for me.

speaker: wilco
sentence: They felt attainable.
citation: Jeff Tweedy, in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2018): "They felt attainable."
note: Also: they "were making music with so few moving parts that you could hear what was going on and learn what each instrument was doing" and "That was liberating for kids like me" -- said of the time he started writing songs and playing shows.

speaker: wire
sentence: We didn’t have anything to do with Gang of Four.
citation: Colin Newman, in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2017): "We didn’t have anything to do with Gang of Four."
note: "They were coming from a very different place."

speaker: xiu-xiu
sentence: It is an homage to Suicide, Einstürzende Neubauten, Nico, and Kraftwerk.

speaker: yo-la-tengo
sentence: At that point, Damaged by Black Flag had great sway over me and to this day it still does.
citation: Yo La Tengo (James McNew, Ira Kaplan, Georgia Hubley), in Pitchfork's 5-10-15-20 (2018): "At that point, Damaged by Black Flag had great sway over me and to this day it still does."
note: James McNew at 15, before joining Yo La Tengo in 1991; "Black Flag were a natural extension of my childhood love of hard rock."
